findings.reason: as written the gate has an unreleasable state that is present in this workspace, so the shipped rule would strand waiters on a done section; the plan needs either a key on the section's latest landed run rather than on every run of it, or a named release for a promoted revision no branch carries, plus a done-when case for it.
findings.text: the Deliverable makes a section's waiters hold until every run of it that has "delivered or been promoted" has its revision in the registered checkout's HEAD, and names only discard or supersede as the releases; a run that was promoted and whose revision then reached no branch at all is neither, so its section's waiters wait with no release route. Measured: run `r-20261110T223806865226-a-design-and-a-content-review-run-together` promoted with `gate: passed` and `promoted_revision 0acd64d90fbc41bca47c11d7170afbd6d7f55f0e`, while `git branch -a --contains 0acd64d9` in `/home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon` names no branch, and that revision is an ancestor of neither `HEAD` nor `origin/main`; its section, `§48` of `a-plan-is-reviewed-before-it-is-built`, is declared `done`, and `~/.config/reckon/crew/discards` (185 records) holds no record for the run, so neither the discard nor the supersede release applies. The same shape arises whenever one section is dispatched twice and an earlier run is promoted and abandoned while a later one lands: the section is genuinely done, yet the abandoned run alone keeps every waiter held. "Superseded" is not a state read from a run's pointer or ledger row (it exists only as an obligation-side notion of a review or resume superseding an earlier head), so a worker implementing the rule as written has nothing to consult for it.

rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the release rule ("does not release its waiters while a run of it is still unlanded") with its stated release list (discard or supersede) leaves a section whose promoted run's revision no branch contains holding its waiters forever, and that state exists on this workstation today.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable, the release of a section wait being gated on the upstream's landing, with the discard/supersede release and the declaration-only section carried as parts of that same gate rather than as separate work.
